subject: Post-demo: deployment decision path & Hosted quickstart
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fintegrate.com>, Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@fintegrate.com>
Cc: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment decision path & Hosted quickstart

Thanks again for a productive demo today — appreciate the candid discussion on throughput and compliance constraints. This thread is a quick recap with suggested next steps so we can converge on the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

Recap (short):
- POC goal: integrate Redwood for customer support summarization + semantic search over redacted ticket text.
- Key constraints: data-in-transit encryption, retention controls, and regional residency for EU customers (Ben flagged ~10% of traffic today).
- Expected POC volume: 200–600 requests/minute during weekday peaks; many requests are short (summary prompts ~150 tokens).

Suggested next steps:
1) Quick Hosted POC: we can provision a Hosted sandbox with 30-day isolated project + strict retention settings and SOC2 controls for initial validation. Aisha will send a one-page quickstart + sample curl flows. (Attachment: rdw_quickstart-instructions.pdf)
2) Rate-limit check: we propose starting with Hosted default limits (see matrix) and run for 2 days to validate tail latency; if sustained traffic patterns exceed 500 rps or you need guaranteed throughput, we look at Dedicated capacity.
3) Security checkpoint: Monica can run through the data residency options and KMS/HSM integration next week.

If that sounds OK I’ll loop in engineering to schedule a 45-minute technical setup on Tue or Wed next week. Please reply with any missing asks or constraints.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference for production LLMs

From: Elena Morales <elena@fintegrate.com>

Cc: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@fintegrate.com>, ops@fintegrate.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment decision path & Hosted quickstart

Thanks Marcus — big thanks to Aisha for the demo. A few clarifying items before we lock in the quickstart: 

1) Data residency: For the POC we can accept US-hosted processing for de-identified ticket text, but any EU customer data must stay in EU. Do you have EU-hosted Hosted projects today or is that Dedicated/Private only?

2) Retention & logs: We need to ensure logs and request bodies can be purged on demand (legal hold exceptions aside). Is that supported in the hosted sandbox?

3) Throughput: The 200–600 reqs/minute is per cluster of agents (we run ~6 clusters), so peak fanout could make sustained higher spikes — say bursts to 1,200 req/minute for 5–10 minutes. What would you recommend to avoid throttling?

4) Endpoints & SDKs: Our infra team prefers a single, stable endpoint (no vendor redirects) and an official Python SDK. You mentioned a streaming path for summaries — can you outline the endpoint names and typical latency expectations?

If you send the quickstart and rate-limit matrix I’ll share with ops and infra for sign-off. Also open to a technical session next Tue afternoon.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Integrations | Fintegrate Systems
elena@fintegrate.com

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fintegrate.com>, Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment decision path & Hosted quickstart

Hi Elena — great questions. I’m Aisha (Solutions Eng). Below are concise answers plus an actionable quickstart plan. I attached the quickstart PDF and a short rate_limit_matrix.csv for easy sharing.

Short answers: 
- EU residency: We have Hosted projects in EU regions (Frankfurt, Dublin) for customers using Hosted. You can request the project to be provisioned in EU and we’ll isolate compute + logs to the region. Private (on-prem) is always an option for full control, and Dedicated provides reserved capacity in the region you choose.

- Retention & purge: Hosted sandbox supports configurable retention windows and on-demand purge for request bodies and traces. Logs that are part of billing traces may have different retention; we’ll document the exact policy for your legal/ops team.

- Throughput & throttling: Hosted default limits (per project) are intended for interactive workloads. Practical guidance: 
  * Default burst: up to 200 requests/second (rps) sustained for short windows.
  * Steady-state: typical soft-limit 60 rps per project; we can raise this for POCs.
  * If you expect sustained >500 rps or deterministic SLAs (no throttling), Dedicated is recommended — reserved GPU pools with autoscaling and guaranteed throughput.
  * For your described pattern (6 clusters, potential 1,200 req/minute bursts), Hosted POC is fine if we configure temporary increased quotas and adaptive throttling with retry headers. If you need completely seamless fanout without retries we should size a Dedicated pool.

- Endpoints & SDKs:
  * REST endpoints (Hosted): POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat for chat-style summaries (streaming supported), POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs for one-shot generation, and POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings for vectors.
  * Python SDK: official package redwoodinference (pip install redwoodinference). Example quickstart in the attached PDF includes a sample streaming call and a non-streaming curl.
  * Latency: median tail for short prompts on Hosted (eu/us) is typically 60–150ms per token for small models and 250–600ms for larger models under light load. We’ll provide model-specific profiled latencies in the follow-up doc.

Quickstart plan (timeline):
- Day 0: We provision a Hosted sandbox project in your preferred region (US for de-id testing; EU for EU traffic).
- Day 1: Exchange API key + KMS info if you want customer-managed keys. We’ll provide sample curl and Python SDK snippets (see rdw_quickstart-instructions.pdf).
- Day 2: Run smoke tests (10–50 qps) and confirm latencies.
- Day 3: Run load run at your expected burst (we can temporarily raise project quotas for the test window).
- Day 4: Review results and recommend either continue Hosted with tuned quotas and caching, or move to Dedicated for reserved capacity.

Security notes: We support TLS1.3, per-project KMS integration, audit logs for all requests, and SOC2 + ISO27001 reports available under NDA.

Attachments included: rdw_quickstart-instructions.pdf, rate_limit_matrix.csv

I’ll be on the Tue technical call — propose Tue Sep 1, 14:00 PT. Marcus, can you confirm?

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
